Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-c) demonstrate diffuse, tiny (micronodular) opacities scattered throughout the lung parenchyma in both upper and lower zones, which is the classic radiographic appearance of miliary tuberculosis. This pattern correlates strongly with the systemic symptoms of prolonged fever and elevated inflammatory markers (increased sedimentation rate) described in option B, whereas the other options describe distinct patterns (large nodules, peribronchovascular distribution, or single mass) not seen here.
